candidate.answerReason: The decreasing line is below the x-axis exactly to the right of its intercept at x=3, giving x>3, choice C.

methods.label: Read the negative side of the intercept
methods.explanation: \(y<0\) corresponds to the graph being below the x-axis. Since \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases, this occurs to the right of the intersection, that is, \(x>3\).
methods.levelReason: The supplied intercept and decreasing behavior allow a direct Grade 8 interpretation of the graph's negative region.

methods.label: Solve using the negative coefficient
methods.explanation: To isolate \(x\), subtract \(3\) from both sides of \(-x+3<0\), giving \(-x<-3\). Dividing both sides by \(-1\) reverses the inequality. Therefore the solution set is \(x>3\), with \(x=3\) excluded, choice C.
methods.levelReason: The alternative uses Grade 7 inequality solving and explicitly applies the direction reversal when dividing by a negative number.
